It has been reported of some reciters that he would lengthen the alif and extend it in "an jāʾahu" (أن جاءه), saying "ā-n jāʾahu" (آن جاءه), as though the meaning in his reading were: "Is it because the blind man came to him? He frowned and turned away," just as one who reads "ān kāna dhā māl wa banīn" (آن كان ذا مال وبنين) with the alif of "an" extended, and another reads it shortened.

It is mentioned that the blind man whom God mentions in this verse is Ibn Umm Maktum, and the Prophet ﷺ was rebuked on account of him.

Mention of the reports transmitted concerning this:

Saʿid ibn Yahya al-Umawi related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from what ʿUrwa presented to him, from ʿAʾisha, who said: "He frowned and turned away" was revealed concerning Ibn Umm Maktum. She said: He came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and began saying: "Guide me." She said: With the Messenger of God ﷺ were some of the great men of the polytheists. She said: The Prophet ﷺ began to turn away from him and to face the other, saying: "Do you see any harm in what I am saying?" He would say: "No." It was concerning this that "He frowned and turned away" was revealed.

Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: "He frowned and turned away, because there came to him the blind man." He said: "While the Messenger of God ﷺ was conversing privately with ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and al-ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, and he would often make himself available to them and present to them that they should believe, a blind man named ʿAbdullah ibn Umm Maktum came toward him, walking while he was conversing with them. ʿAbdullah began asking the Prophet ﷺ to recite a verse of the Qur'an to him and said: 'O Messenger of God, teach me of what God has taught you.' The Messenger of God ﷺ turned away from him, frowned at his face, turned aside, disliked his speech, and faced the others. When the Messenger of God ﷺ had finished and began to return to his family, God withdrew some of his sight, then he lowered his head, and God revealed: 'He frowned and turned away, because there came to him the blind man. And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself, or be reminded, so the reminder would benefit him.' When this was revealed concerning him, the Messenger of God ﷺ honored him, spoke to him, and said to him: 'What is your need? Do you want anything?' And whenever he left his presence, he would say to him: 'Is there anything you need?' This was when God revealed: 'As for one who considers himself self-sufficient, you give him attention, though it is not upon you that he should not purify himself.'"

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Hisham, from his father, who said: "He frowned and turned away, because there came to him the blind man" was revealed concerning Ibn Umm Maktum.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's words: "because there came to him the blind man," who said: "A man from the Banu Fihr, called Ibn Umm Maktum."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, regarding "He frowned and turned away, because there came to him the blind man": "ʿAbdullah ibn Zaʾida, who is Ibn Umm Maktum, came to him seeking to be taught, while he was conversing with Umayya ibn Khalaf, a man of the nobility of Quraysh. The Prophet of God ﷺ turned away from him, so God revealed concerning him what you hear: 'He frowned and turned away, because there came to him the blind man,' up to His words: 'So you are distracted from him.'" It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God ﷺ later appointed him as his deputy over Medina twice, during two campaigns he undertook, leading the prayer for its people.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik, that he saw him on the day of al-Qadisiyya carrying a black banner, and wearing his armor.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, who said: Ibn Umm Maktum came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was speaking with Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and he turned away from him, so God revealed to him: "He frowned and turned away." After that the Prophet ﷺ would honor him. Anas said: I saw him on the day of al-Qadisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black banner.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words, "He frowned and turned away": The Messenger of God ﷺ made himself available to a man of the polytheists of Quraysh who had much wealth, hoping he would believe. A man of the Ansar who was blind, called ʿAbdullah ibn Umm Maktum, came and began asking the Prophet of God ﷺ, and the Prophet of God ﷺ disliked him and turned away from him, facing the wealthy man. So God admonished His Prophet, and the Prophet of God ﷺ honored him and appointed him as his deputy over Medina twice, during two campaigns he undertook.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, and I asked him about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: "He frowned and turned away, because there came to him the blind man." He said: Ibn Umm Maktum came to the Messenger of God ﷺ with his guide, while he could see, and he could not see. He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was gesturing to his guide to restrain him, while Ibn Umm Maktum pushed him and could not see. He said: Until the Messenger of God ﷺ frowned, and God rebuked him for that, saying: "He frowned and turned away, because there came to him the blind man. And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself..." up to His words: "So you are distracted from him." Ibn Zayd said: It used to be said: If the Messenger of God ﷺ had concealed anything of the revelation, he would have concealed this for himself. He said: He used to make himself available to this nobleman in his jahiliyya, hoping he would become Muslim, and from this he was distracted.

God, exalted is His mention, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "And what would make you know, O Muhammad, perhaps this blind man at whose face you frowned would purify himself," meaning: would cleanse himself of his sins.

Ibn Zayd used to say concerning this:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, "Perhaps he would purify himself": "He would become Muslim."

*Perhaps the vicissitudes of time or its turns / Will give us victory over its afflictions,*
*So the soul will rest from its sighs, / And the thirst will be quenched from its springs.*

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, regarding "He frowned and turned away, because there came to him the blind man": "ʿAbdullah ibn Zaʾida, who is Ibn Umm Maktum, came to him seeking to be taught, while he was conversing with Umayya ibn Khalaf, a man of the nobility of Quraysh. The Prophet of God ﷺ turned away from him, so God revealed concerning him what you hear: 'He frowned and turned away, because there came to him the blind man,' up to His words: 'So you are distracted from him.'" It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God ﷺ later appointed him as his deputy over Medina twice, during two campaigns he undertook, leading the prayer for its people.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik, that he saw him on the day of al-Qadisiyya carrying a black banner, and wearing his armor.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, who said: Ibn Umm Maktum came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was speaking with Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and he turned away from him, so God revealed to him: "He frowned and turned away." After that the Prophet ﷺ would honor him. Anas said: I saw him on the day of al-Qadisiyya wearing armor and carrying a black banner.

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words, "He frowned and turned away": The Messenger of God ﷺ made himself available to a man of the polytheists of Quraysh who had much wealth, hoping he would believe. A man of the Ansar who was blind, called ʿAbdullah ibn Umm Maktum, came and began asking the Prophet of God ﷺ, and the Prophet of God ﷺ disliked him and turned away from him, facing the wealthy man. So God admonished His Prophet, and the Prophet of God ﷺ honored him and appointed him as his deputy over Medina twice, during two campaigns he undertook.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, and I asked him about the words of God, Mighty and Majestic: "He frowned and turned away, because there came to him the blind man." He said: Ibn Umm Maktum came to the Messenger of God ﷺ with his guide, while he could see, and he could not see. He said: The Messenger of God ﷺ was gesturing to his guide to restrain him, while Ibn Umm Maktum pushed him and could not see. He said: Until the Messenger of God ﷺ frowned, and God rebuked him for that, saying: "He frowned and turned away, because there came to him the blind man. And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself..." up to His words: "So you are distracted from him." Ibn Zayd said: It used to be said: If the Messenger of God ﷺ had concealed anything of the revelation, he would have concealed this for himself. He said: He used to make himself available to this nobleman in his jahiliyya, hoping he would become Muslim, and from this he was distracted.

* *

As for His words: "And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself":

God, exalted is His mention, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "And what would make you know, O Muhammad, perhaps this blind man at whose face you frowned would purify himself," meaning: would cleanse himself of his sins.

Ibn Zayd used to say concerning this:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, "Perhaps he would purify himself": "He would become Muslim."

* *

As for His words: "Or be reminded, so the reminder would benefit him":

It means: or he would be mindful, so the reminder would benefit him, i.e., he would take heed, and admonition and exhortation would benefit him. The reading "fa-tanfaʿahu" (فتنفعه) with a nominative ending is coordinated with His words "yadhdhakkaru" (يَذَّكَّرُ). It has been transmitted from ʿAsim that both the accusative and nominative are read in it. The accusative is read by making it a response introduced by "fa" after "laʿalla" (لعل), as the poet said:

*Perhaps the vicissitudes of time or its turns / Will give us victory over its afflictions,*
*So the soul will rest from its sighs, / And the thirst will be quenched from its springs.*

"Wa-tunqaʿ" (وتُنْقَعُ) is transmitted with both nominative and accusative endings.

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿As for him who thinks himself self-sufficient (5), to him you attend eagerly (6). Yet it is not your responsibility if he does not purify himself (7). But as for him who comes to you eagerly (8), and fears (Allah) (9), from him you are distracted (10).﴾

.

Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): As for him who thinks himself self-sufficient through his wealth, you give him your attention, hoping that he will become Muslim.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, regarding ﴿As for him who thinks himself self-sufficient, to him you attend eagerly﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning al-Abbas.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿As for him who thinks himself self-sufficient﴾, he said: (It refers to) Utba ibn Rabi'a and Shayba ibn Rabi'a. ﴿Yet it is not your responsibility if he does not purify himself﴾ means: What is it to you if he does not purify himself of his disbelief and become Muslim? ﴿But as for him who comes to you eagerly﴾ means: As for this blind man who came to you eagerly, ﴿and fears (Allah)﴾, meaning he fears Allah and is mindful of Him, ﴿from him you are distracted﴾ means: you turn away from him and occupy yourself with others and neglect him.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿No! Indeed, it is a reminder (11). So whoever wills may remember it (12) in scriptures held in honor (13), exalted and purified (14), by the hands of scribes (15), noble and righteous (16). Destroyed is man; how disbelieving he is! (17).﴾

.

Exalted is He, says: ﴿No!﴾ The matter is not as you do, O Muhammad, by frowning at the one who comes to you eagerly while fearing (Allah), and attending to the one who thinks himself self-sufficient. ﴿Indeed, it is a reminder﴾ means: Indeed, this admonition and this surah are a reminder, meaning an admonition and a lesson. ﴿So whoever wills may remember it﴾ means: whoever among the servants of Allah wills, may remember it, meaning remember the revelation and inspiration of Allah. The pronoun in His saying "innaha" (indeed it) refers to the surah, and the pronoun in His saying "dhakarahu" (may remember it) refers to the revelation and inspiration. ﴿In scriptures﴾ means: it is a reminder ﴿in scriptures held in honor, exalted and purified﴾, meaning: in the Preserved Tablet, which is exalted and purified with Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿by the hands of scribes﴾

It means: the scriptures held in honor are in the hands of scribes, plural of safir (scribe/messenger).

The exegetes differed concerning who they are. Some of them said: they are scribes (kataba).

Those who said this:

⁕ Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿by the hands of scribes﴾, he said: scribes.

⁕ Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿by the hands of scribes﴾, he said: the scribes.

Others said: they are the reciters (qurra').

Those who said this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿so whoever wills may remember it, in scriptures held in honor, exalted and purified, by the hands of scribes﴾, he said: they are the reciters.

Others said: they are the angels.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿by the hands of scribes, noble and righteous﴾, he meant: the angels.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿by the hands of scribes, noble and righteous﴾: The safara are those who count the deeds.

The most correct of these interpretations is the view of those who said: they are the angels who act as intermediaries (yasfirun) between Allah and His messengers with the revelation.

The safir of a people is the one who goes between them to make peace. It is said: "safartu bayna al-qawm" (I mediated between the people) when one reconciles them. From this is the saying of the poet:

"And I do not abandon mediation among my people, and I do not walk with deceit if I walk [between them]."

[Footnote from the editor: the chain is sound; Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz, Tabari's teacher, was criticized over one hadith, but the truth is that he is acceptable, as al-Daraqutni said. Abu Asim is al-Nabil, al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad, the hafiz and proof. Shabib is Ibn Bishr al-Bajali; the printed Tahdhib has "al-Halabi," a typographical error, the correct form appearing in al-Tarikh al-Kabir of al-Bukhari and al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil of Ibn Abi Hatim, and he is trustworthy, as Ibn Ma'in declared.]

And when the interpretation is directed toward what we have said, both opinions are possible: the view of those who said they are scribes, and the view of those who said they are reciters, since the angels are the ones who read the books and act as intermediaries between Allah and His messengers.

As for His saying: ﴿noble and righteous﴾

"Barara" is the plural of barr (righteous), just as "kafara" is the plural of kafir and "saharа" of sahir. * *

As for His saying: ﴿Destroyed is man; how disbelieving he is!﴾

Exalted is He says: Cursed is the disbelieving man, how disbelieving he is.

Mujahid said something similar to what we have said.

⁕ Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, who said: Whatever in the Qur'an says "qutila al-insan" (destroyed is man) or "fu'ila bil-insan" (was done to man), it refers only to the disbeliever.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 80, verse 24–30:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So let man look at his food﴾ [24] ﴿That We poured down water in torrents﴾ [25] ﴿Then We split the earth in splitting﴾ [26] ﴿And caused to grow therein grain﴾ [27] ﴿And grapes and herbage﴾ [28] ﴿And olive and palm trees﴾ [29] ﴿And gardens of dense trees﴾ [30]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Let this man, the disbeliever who denies the oneness of God, look at his food, how He arranged it.

As related:

• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So let man look at his food﴾: "and his drink" — he said: "at his eating and his drinking."

• Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his words ﴿So let man look at his food﴾: "a sign for them."

Scholars of interpretation have said what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

• Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Muawiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And herbage﴾: he said: "al-fisfisa" (clover).

• Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And herbage﴾: he said: "And qadb: al-fasafis" (clover).

Abu Ja'far, may God have mercy on him, said: al-fisfisa is the fresh green fodder (al-ratba).

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿And herbage﴾: it means fresh fodder.

• Bishr related to us, saying: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad related to us, saying: Yunus related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And herbage﴾: he said: "qadb: fodder (al-alaf)."

* *

As for His words ﴿And olive﴾:

This is the olive from which oil is made. ﴿And palm trees﴾ and ﴿gardens of dense trees﴾. We have already explained that a hadiqa is an enclosed orchard.

* *

As for His words ﴿Gardens of dense trees (ghulban)﴾:

It means: massive. And by His words ﴿ghulban﴾ is meant trees in thick-trunked gardens.

Ghulb is the plural of aghlab, which is a man with a thick neck. From this is the verse of al-Farazdaq:

"He howled and stirred up a thick-necked lion, so woe to the son of al-Maragha for what he stirred up!"

Scholars of interpretation have said, in line with what we have said, though they differ in explaining it. Some of them said: it is what is intertwined and gathered of trees.

Those who said so:

• Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from Asim ibn Kulayb, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And gardens of dense trees﴾: he said: "al-hada'iq: what is intertwined and gathered."

• Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And gardens of dense trees﴾: he said: "good (tayyiba)."

Others said: al-hada'iq: all kinds of trees.

Those who said so:

• Abu Hisham related to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, saying: Isam related to us, from his father: "al-hada'iq: all kinds of trees."

• Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Shabib, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And gardens of dense trees﴾: he said: "trees under whose shade one rests in Paradise."

Others said: rather, ghulb means: tall.

Those who said so:

• Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Muawiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And gardens of dense trees﴾: he said: "tall."

Others said: it is noble palm trees.

Those who said so:

• Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And gardens of dense trees﴾: "ghulb: noble palm trees."

• Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And gardens of dense trees﴾: he said: "noble palm trees."

• Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And gardens of dense trees﴾: "great palm trees with large trunks." He said: "And ghulb among men: those with thick necks; it is said: he is aghlab al-raqaba, meaning: thick of neck."

• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from his father, from Ikrima, regarding ﴿gardens of dense trees﴾: he said: "massive middles."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 80, verse 24–30:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So let man look at his food﴾ [24] ﴿That We poured down water in torrents﴾ [25] ﴿Then We split the earth in splitting﴾ [26] ﴿And caused to grow therein grain﴾ [27] ﴿And grapes and herbage﴾ [28] ﴿And olive and palm trees﴾ [29] ﴿And gardens of dense trees﴾ [30]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Let this man, the disbeliever who denies the oneness of God, look at his food, how He arranged it.

As related:

• Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So let man look at his food﴾: "and his drink" — he said: "at his eating and his drinking."

• Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his words ﴿So let man look at his food﴾: "a sign for them."

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿That We poured down water in torrents﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read "anna" with a kasra on the alif, as a resumed statement (isti'naf). The majority of the reciters of Kufa read "anna" with a fatha on the alif, meaning: "let man look at food, [namely] that We..." so that "anna" is in a genitive position by implication of repeating the governing preposition. It may also be permissible for it to be in the nominative when vowelled with a fatha, by taking it as an apposition to "ta'amihi" (his food).

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that both are well-known recitations; whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And fruit and herbage (abban), (31) provision for you and your cattle. (36) For every man among them that Day will be a matter that occupies him. (37) Faces that Day will be radiant, (38) laughing, joyful. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿wa-fakihatan﴾ is what people eat of the fruits of trees, and the abb is what livestock eat of grass and plants.

Those who engage in interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said things similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿wa-fakihah﴾, he said: what the son of Adam eats.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿wa-fakihah﴾, he said: what people eat.

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿wa-fakihah﴾, he said: As for the fruit, it is for you.

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿wa-fakihah﴾, he said: The fruit is for us.

* Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, he said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Humayd narrated to us, Anas ibn Malik said: Umar recited ﴿'Abasa wa-tawalla﴾ until he reached this verse ﴿wa-fakihatan wa-abba﴾, and he said: We already know what the fruit is, so what is the abb? Then I think he [al-Tabari, expressing doubt] said: Indeed, this is surely over-formality (al-takalluf).

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, recited ﴿'Abasa wa-tawalla﴾, and when he reached this verse ﴿wa-fakihatan wa-abba﴾, he said: We know the fruit. So what is the abb? He said: By your life, O son of al-Khattab, this is indeed over-formality.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Musa ibn Anas, from Anas, who said: Umar recited ﴿wa-fakihatan wa-abba﴾ while he had a staff in his hand, and he said: What is the abb? Then he said: What we already know is sufficient for us, and he threw the staff from his hand.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khulayd ibn Ja'far, from Abu Iyas Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from Anas, from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Indeed, this is over-formality.

He said: Qatadah narrated to me, from Anas, from Umar, with a similar report in full.

* Abu Kurayb, Abu al-Sa'ib and Ya'qub narrated to us, they said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said: I heard 'Asim ibn Kulayb, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He counted seven, [saying] He made His provision in seven and made it from seven, and at the end of that he said: The abb is what the earth produces that people do not eat.

* Abu Hisham narrated to us, he said: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, he said: 'Asim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The abb is the vegetation of the earth that livestock eat and people do not eat.

* Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, they said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Abbas counted, and said: The abb is what the earth produces for the livestock. This is the wording of Abu Kurayb's report. Abu al-Sa'ib said in his report: He said: What the earth produces that people eat and livestock eat.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The abb is pasture and all grazing.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, who said: The abb is vegetation.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, the like of it.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash or other, from Mujahid, who said: The abb is pasture.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: Mujahid said: ﴿wa-abban﴾ is pasture.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, ﴿wa-abban﴾, he said: The abb is what livestock eat.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying ﴿wa-abban﴾, he said: The abb is what livestock ate.

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: As for the abb, it is for your livestock, blessings from Allah in abundance.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, he said: Yunus narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿wa-abban﴾, he said: The abb is herbage.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan and Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿wa-abban﴾, he said: It is what the beasts eat.

* It was reported to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿wa-abban﴾, meaning: pasture.

* Yunus narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿wa-abban﴾, he said: The abb is for our livestock, and the abb is what is grazed. And he recited: ﴿provision for you and your cattle﴾.

He said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Yunus and 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that Anas ibn Malik told him that he heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, say: Allah said: ﴿wa-qadban wa-zaytunan wa-nakhlan wa-hada'iqa ghulba wa-fakihatan wa-abba﴾. All of this we already know, so what is the abb? Then he struck with his hand, then said: By your life, this is indeed over-formality. Follow what becomes clear to you in this Book, and whatever becomes clear to you, act upon it, and what does not, leave it.

Others said: The abb is juicy fruits.

Mention of those who said that:

* 'Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿wa-abban﴾, he said: The juicy fruits.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿provision for you﴾

He means: We caused these things that the children of Adam eat to grow as provision for you, O people, and a benefit by which you enjoy and profit, and those that livestock eat are for your livestock. The root of an-na'am is camels, then it is used for every grazing animal (ra'iyah).

Those who engage in interpretation have said similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿provision for you and your cattle﴾, he said: Provision for you is the fruit, and for your livestock is the herbage.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿So when the Deafening Blast comes﴾

It is mentioned that it is one of the names of the Resurrection, and I think it is derived from the expression "sakha fulan li-sawt fulan" (so-and-so was attentive to so-and-so's voice), meaning: he listened to him. But from this one says "huwa musikh lahu" (he is attentive to him). Perhaps the sound is the Sakhkh (the deafening blast), and if that is so, then it should be that before it there is the blast of the Trumpet.

Mention of those who said: It is one of the names of the Resurrection:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿wa-fakihah﴾, he said: what people eat.

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿wa-fakihah﴾, he said: As for the fruit, it is for you.

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿wa-fakihah﴾, he said: The fruit is for us.

* Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, he said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Humayd narrated to us, Anas ibn Malik said: Umar recited ﴿'Abasa wa-tawalla﴾ until he reached this verse ﴿wa-fakihatan wa-abba﴾, and he said: We already know what the fruit is, so what is the abb? Then I think he [al-Tabari, expressing doubt] said: Indeed, this is surely over-formality (al-takalluf).

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Humayd, from Anas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, recited ﴿'Abasa wa-tawalla﴾, and when he reached this verse ﴿wa-fakihatan wa-abba﴾, he said: We know the fruit. So what is the abb? He said: By your life, O son of al-Khattab, this is indeed over-formality.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Musa ibn Anas, from Anas, who said: Umar recited ﴿wa-fakihatan wa-abba﴾ while he had a staff in his hand, and he said: What is the abb? Then he said: What we already know is sufficient for us, and he threw the staff from his hand.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, he said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khulayd ibn Ja'far, from Abu Iyas Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from Anas, from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Indeed, this is over-formality.

He said: Qatadah narrated to me, from Anas, from Umar, with a similar report in full.

* Abu Kurayb, Abu al-Sa'ib and Ya'qub narrated to us, they said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said: I heard 'Asim ibn Kulayb, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He counted seven, [saying] He made His provision in seven and made it from seven, and at the end of that he said: The abb is what the earth produces that people do not eat.

* Abu Hisham narrated to us, he said: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, he said: 'Asim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The abb is the vegetation of the earth that livestock eat and people do not eat.

* Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, they said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Abbas counted, and said: The abb is what the earth produces for the livestock. This is the wording of Abu Kurayb's report. Abu al-Sa'ib said in his report: He said: What the earth produces that people eat and livestock eat.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: My paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The abb is pasture and all grazing.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, who said: The abb is vegetation.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu Razin, the like of it.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash or other, from Mujahid, who said: The abb is pasture.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: Mujahid said: ﴿wa-abban﴾ is pasture.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Waki' narrated to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, ﴿wa-abban﴾, he said: The abb is what livestock eat.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying ﴿wa-abban﴾, he said: The abb is what livestock ate.

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: As for the abb, it is for your livestock, blessings from Allah in abundance.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, he said: Yunus narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿wa-abban﴾, he said: The abb is herbage.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan and Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿wa-abban﴾, he said: It is what the beasts eat.

* It was reported to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿wa-abban﴾, meaning: pasture.

* Yunus narrated to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿wa-abban﴾, he said: The abb is for our livestock, and the abb is what is grazed. And he recited: ﴿provision for you and your cattle﴾.

He said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Yunus and 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that Anas ibn Malik told him that he heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, say: Allah said: ﴿wa-qadban wa-zaytunan wa-nakhlan wa-hada'iqa ghulba wa-fakihatan wa-abba﴾. All of this we already know, so what is the abb? Then he struck with his hand, then said: By your life, this is indeed over-formality. Follow what becomes clear to you in this Book, and whatever becomes clear to you, act upon it, and what does not, leave it.

Others said: The abb is juicy fruits.

Mention of those who said that:

* 'Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿wa-abban﴾, he said: The juicy fruits.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿provision for you﴾

He means: We caused these things that the children of Adam eat to grow as provision for you, O people, and a benefit by which you enjoy and profit, and those that livestock eat are for your livestock. The root of an-na'am is camels, then it is used for every grazing animal (ra'iyah).

Those who engage in interpretation have said similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿provision for you and your cattle﴾, he said: Provision for you is the fruit, and for your livestock is the herbage.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿So when the Deafening Blast comes﴾

It is mentioned that it is one of the names of the Resurrection, and I think it is derived from the expression "sakha fulan li-sawt fulan" (so-and-so was attentive to so-and-so's voice), meaning: he listened to him. But from this one says "huwa musikh lahu" (he is attentive to him). Perhaps the sound is the Sakhkh (the deafening blast), and if that is so, then it should be that before it there is the blast of the Trumpet.

Mention of those who said: It is one of the names of the Resurrection:

* 'Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿So when the Deafening Blast comes﴾, he said: This is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, which Allah magnified and warned His servants of.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿on the Day a man flees from his brother﴾

He says: So when the Deafening Blast comes on this Day on which a man flees from his brother. By His saying "flees from his brother" he means: flees away from his brother ﴿and his mother and his father and his spouse﴾, meaning: his wife who was his wife in the world, ﴿and his children﴾, out of fear of their demanding from him what lies between him and them of obligations and wrongs.

Some of them said: The meaning of His saying ﴿a man flees from his brother﴾ is that he flees from his brother so as not to see him, and what befalls him. ﴿For every man﴾ means: of the man and his brother and his mother and his father, and all others mentioned in this verse. ﴿On that Day﴾ means: the Day of Resurrection, when the Deafening Blast comes on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿A matter that occupies him﴾ means: a matter that occupies him and diverts him from the concerns of others.

As:

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿For every man among them that Day will be a matter that occupies him﴾: it has come upon each person what preoccupies him from people.

* Abu 'Umarah al-Marwazi al-Husayn ibn Hurayth narrated to us, he said: al-Fadl ibn Musa narrated to us, from 'A'idh ibn Shurayh, from Anas, who said: 'A'ishah asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, she said: O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, I want to ask you about a matter you told me about. He said: "If I have knowledge of it." She said: O Prophet of Allah, how will men be gathered? He said: "Barefoot, naked." Then she waited an hour and said: O Prophet of Allah, how will women be gathered? He said: "Likewise, barefoot, naked." She said: Alas for my shame on the Day of Resurrection! He said: "And about that you ask me? Indeed a verse has been revealed to me that does not harm you whether you have garments or not." She said: What verse is it, O Prophet of Allah? He said: ﴿For every man among them that Day will be a matter that occupies him﴾.

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding the saying of Allah ﴿For every man among them that Day will be a matter that occupies him﴾: a matter that has preoccupied him from his companion.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: faces that Day will be bright and luminous, and they are the faces of the believers with whom Allah is pleased. It is said: "asfara wajhu fulan" when his face became beautiful; and from it "asfara al-subh" when it shone; and everything luminous is musfir. As for safara without the alif, it is said of a woman when she casts her veil from her face or her face-cover; it is said: "qad safarat al-mar'ah 'an wajhiha" when she does that, and she is safir. From it is the saying of Tawbah ibn al-Humayyir:

And when I visited Layla she would veil herself,
but her unveiling this morning has troubled me.

[Editor's note: the chain to Mujahid is weak, as Sufyan (al-Thawri) did not hear from Mujahid; the report is likely an error of Mihran ibn Abi Umar, whose reports from al-Thawri contain confusion. It is also cited by Ibn Kathir without chain and by al-Suyuti, attributing it also to 'Abd ibn Humayd.]

He means by "unveiling" (sufur): casting her face-cover from her face.

﴿Laughing﴾ means: laughing from the joy of the blessings and honour Allah has given them, ﴿joyful﴾ for what they hope of increase.

Those who engage in interpretation have said similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of ﴿radiant﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

* 'Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿radiant﴾, he said: shining.

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, laughing, joyful﴾: these are the people of Paradise.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿And faces that Day will have dust upon them﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And faces﴾, which are the faces of the disbelievers, that Day have dust upon them. It is mentioned that the beasts which Allah turns into dust that Day, after the judgment between them, that dust becomes dust-colour on the faces of the people of disbelief. ﴿Covered by darkness﴾ means: those faces are covered by darkness, which is the dust.

Those who engage in interpretation have said similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

* 'Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿covered by darkness﴾, he said: overtaken by humiliation.

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿covered by darkness﴾: these are the faces of the people of Hell. He said: al-qatarah is from al-ghabarah, and they are one and the same. He said: As for in this world, al-qatarah is what rises and reaches the sky, and the wind lifts it; the Arabs call it al-qatarah, and what is lower on the earth is al-ghabarah.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those who have this description on the Day of Resurrection are the disbelievers in Allah; they were in the world the wicked in their religion, not caring what they committed of disobedience to Allah, and engaging in what He has forbidden; so Allah requited them for the evil of their deeds with what He informed His servants of.

End of the commentary on Surah 'Abasa.
